title: Queue cohort optimizer with SLO mitigations and staged rollback
creator: Maya Liu
description: Implement a cohort-based queue optimizer that recommends batching and caching configurations per traffic cohort, applies changes safely via staged shadow-apply and traffic-slicing, and provides automated rollback when latency/throughput SLOs degrade. This ticket covers the algorithm prototype, config application orchestration, anomaly detection thresholds, and integration points for Console dashboards and rollout policies.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype produces per-cohort recommendations (batch size, prefix cache TTL, QoS token rate) from historical trace/sample windows
Apply plan supports: dry-run shadow-apply, low-ratio canary (1-5%), ramp to target with ramp windows, and automated rollback trigger
Anomaly detector flags SLO regressions within 3 standard deviations over rolling 5-minute windows and signals orchestrator
Console shows cohort-level expected cost delta, predicted p95 latency impact, and rollout progress with automatic remediation links
Integration test validates that a simulated spike causes staged rollback within configured SLA (10s) in CI harness
proposed_solution_summary: Create a lightweight cohorter that slices incoming traffic by model+route+promoted-customer or inferred latency fingerprint. For each cohort compute recommended batching/caching/QoS profile using an objective function (expected token cost reduction subject to p95 latency uplift <= configured SLO delta). Changes are applied via a 4-step orchestrator: 1) shadow-apply to mirror traffic without serving, 2) micro-canary at 1% for 10 minutes, 3) ramp with adaptive gating based on SLO signal, 4) full apply. A separate anomaly detector uses rolling quantile drift and a small AR(1) residual model to detect subtle latency/throughput shifts and trigger rollback. All operations emit events to Console and can be overridden by manual aborts.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Risk: Over-segmentation of cohorts yields noisy signals — mitigated by minimum cohort volume threshold and adaptive grouping
Tradeoff: Conservative SLO deltas reduce cost savings; aggressive deltas increase rollback frequency — default to conservative for first rollout
Risk: Shadow-apply instrumentation adds overhead; isolate sampling to <0.5% of traffic and perform offloaded metric aggregation
Tradeoff: Using AR(1) residuals is lightweight but may miss non-linear regressions — plan for later upgrade to small ensemble detector if false negatives observed
implementation_notes: Cohorter: use existing trace attributes; fall back to route+model if customer tag absent
Objective function defined in cost-optimizer service; ensure deterministic recommendations for auditability
Orchestrator: extend rollout-controller API to accept 'shadow' target and dynamic gating rules
Anomaly detector: implement as sidecar job reading aggregated metrics (p50/p95/tokens/sec) from metrics pipeline
Metrics/Events: add cohort tag to rollout events, include decision rationale and recommended parameters
Integrations: Console UI needs a single-pane summary + link to detailed cohort chart; add a webhook endpoint for Slack alerts
